lines.text: In two thousand and eight, thieves in Jamaica pulled off one of the strangest crimes ever -
by stealing an entire four-hundred-meter white sand beach overnight.
In the tropical bay of Coral Spring, developers were building a multi-million-dollar luxury beach resort.
The property was famous for its rare, sugar-white coral sand.
Then one morning, project managers showed up to work and stood in disbelief.
Under the cover of darkness, an organized convoy of heavy excavators and dump trucks had arrived in secret.
They scooped up five hundred truckloads - over four thousand metric tons of precious white sand,
leaving behind nothing but jagged, barren limestone rocks facing the Caribbean ocean.
The stolen sand was worth hundreds of thousands of dollars on the black market.
Jamaica's Prime Minister ordered an urgent national task force, suspecting rival hotels bought the sand to pave their own private shores.
Yet to this day, not a single grain of sand was ever recovered, making it the most audacious environmental heist in history.
